status.description: developed: the student explains the point with at least one reason, example or consequence of their own that SUPPORTS it. restated: the point is mentioned (read, paraphrased or named) but nothing is added in its support. not_addressed: not mentioned. misread: presented on the wrong side or with a meaning the point does not have.

rebutted.description: true when the student states this point only to argue against it ('Some people say X, but…').

evidence.description: Exact substring of the transcript where the point is made, or ''.

development_evidence.description: Exact substring with the student's own reason or example SUPPORTING this point, or '' unless developed. A rebuttal is never this point's development.

note.description: One short sentence for the student about this point.

model_answer.description: For restated / not_addressed points: 1–2 sentences (at most 40 words) developing it at C1, on this point only. '' otherwise.

points.description: Exactly F1, F2, F3, A1, A2, A3, in this order.

evidence.description: Exact substring: an argument of the student's own that is not on the list.
Exact substrings that show reading or leaning on the prompt text; [] for own_development.

coherent_and_sustained.description: false when the answer is a list of fragments rather than a connected argument.

evidence.description: Exact substrings copied from the transcript. Never paraphrase.

note.description: One short sentence for the student: why this level, referring to the quotes.

how_to_improve.description: One concrete instruction for the next attempt, about ONE issue. Examples on another topic.

how_to_check.description: How the student can tell, after the next attempt, that they did it. A skill, never a set phrase.

quote.description: Exact substring of the transcript containing the error.

correction.description: The same words, corrected. Keep the student's meaning.

pattern.description: The name of the error pattern in error_patterns this error belongs to (copied exactly), or an empty string for a one-off error.

name.description: Short name of a repeated error type, e.g. 'Missing -s after he/she/it'.

rule.description: One sentence explaining the rule, with a short correct example.

how_to_fix.description: One concrete habit for the next attempt that prevents this error.

quote.description: Exact substring that shows C1-or-better language for this feature.

strengths.description: 0-2 strengths, only for features judged C1 or above_C1.

summary.description: Honest comparison with the previous attempt. Never invent improvement.

you_said.description: The student's own words, copied exactly from the transcript with the mistake in them: one clause or sentence, at most 25 words.

better.description: The same words with ONLY that one mistake fixed. Keep the student's words, order and idea. Never add an idea, a reason or an example; at most 3 words longer. Never a rewritten answer.

why.description: One short line (at most 20 words) naming the rule, in plain words. About grammar or word choice only.

sentence_fixes.description: Up to 8 sentences or phrases of the student's own words with one mistake each, most important first (a mistake that hides the meaning, or one that repeats, before a small slip). Empty list if there is no clear mistake. Without audio, never about pauses, fillers, speed or pronunciation.
